title: Ferret manifest file
description: Structural validation for manifest/NN-name.json. The meaning lives in docs/design/MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md; where the two disagree, that is a bug. This file cannot express the cross-file rules -- duplicate ids, dangling tainted_by, cycles, interpolation tokens, remedy-required-unless-info -- because they need the whole manifest set in view. Those are enforced by the loader, and both run before any probe executes. See MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md section 8.

checks.description: May be empty. An empty layer file is legal and means 'nothing here yet'.

command.description: POSIX sh, executed with sh -c. An array is joined with newlines and passed as one script, so a long probe stays readable in JSON.

id.description: Unique across the whole manifest, not per file. tainted_by references are global. This is the join key across evidence.json, status.md, and the taint DAG.

layer.description: Almost always omitted; inherited from the file. Present only when a check genuinely belongs to a different layer than the file storing it -- rare enough to deserve a notes explaining it.

title.description: One line, rendered verbatim. Write the subject, not the outcome: 'Node version matches pin', never 'Node version is wrong'. The state supplies the outcome.

applies_if.description: Exit 0 means the check applies. Non-zero means N/A -- the probe never runs. A dirty failure (timeout, denylist refusal) is UNKNOWN(probe_error), never N/A.

probe.description: The command whose output is the actual state. A non-zero exit is not a failure; expect decides what the exit code means.

declared.description: The command whose output is the expected state, read from the repo. Separate from expect because nearly every check here is declared-vs-actual, so the comparison lives once in the verdict engine.

severity.description: Describes the failure, not the check. A GO check has no severity in the output.

decisive.description: Whether this check participates in the top-line verdict. Defaults true for blocker, false otherwise. A non-decisive UNKNOWN does not produce exit code 2; a decisive one always does.

tainted_by.description: Prerequisite ids. Edges point upward, declared on the dependent, so adding a check never requires editing an unrelated one. The probe still runs and its output is still recorded -- taint is a judgment about trustworthiness, not a reason to skip collection.

remedy.description: Required unless severity is info -- enforced by the loader, not here. A check that reports breakage without an action is half a tool. A wrong remedy is worse than none.

timeout_s.description: Wall-clock ceiling per command; applies_if, probe, and declared each get the full budget separately. Default 10. Anything touching the network should set this deliberately -- the machines that hang are the ones being diagnosed.

redact.description: Applied at capture time in the runner, before anything is written. A value that never enters evidence.json cannot leak out of it. Levels agree with scripts/lib/redact.sh.

oneOf.description: true is identity; false is standard capture with global redaction still applied.
identity strips user/home/tmpdir/repo. secret is a different rule, not a stronger pass: presence and shape only, never the value.

mutating.description: The mutation denylist escape hatch. Only false is legal -- there is no mutating: true, because a check that admits to mutating does not belong in phase 1. Requires mutating_why.

mutating_why.description: Justification for the override, in the file, next to it. An override without a stated reason is how a denylist rots.

volatility.description: Per docs/design/DOCS_MODEL.md section 3. The runner ignores this; it governs how long a derived claim stays trustworthy in system.md. Specified now so M10 need not change the schema after eighty checks exist.

notes.description: JSON has no comments and a probe that needs explaining should carry the explanation. Nothing reads this.

allOf.description: mutating and mutating_why travel together, in both directions.

expect.description: Read by the verdict engine only. The runner never sees this -- knowing what counts as passing is exactly the interpretation it is forbidden to do. An unevaluable predicate is UNKNOWN(probe_error), never NO-GO: 'the check is broken' and 'the machine is broken' are different findings.

then.description: Exact comparison after trimming both operands. Internal whitespace is significant.
Go regexp (RE2), unanchored unless the pattern anchors itself. An invalid pattern is a load-time validation error, not a runtime UNKNOWN.
Spelled separately rather than as invert on non_empty, because an inverted presence check reads backwards at the call site and the manifest is meant to be skimmable.
Non-numeric input is UNKNOWN(probe_error), not NO-GO -- a probe returning 'command not found' on stdout is Ferret's bug, not a disk-space finding.

Supported syntax is deliberately small: prefix, ^, ~, comparators, || , *. Anything beyond it is UNKNOWN(probe_error) with the unparsed range in the reason, never a guess. An empty range -- a declared that found nothing -- is also UNKNOWN: nothing was declared, so nothing can be satisfied, and that is a different fact from a wrong version.

The escape hatch, used sparingly. Every use is logic that moved from the manifest into shell, where it is neither validated nor re-runnable against old evidence. When it is the honest answer, say why in notes.
